title: Christian Bale reveals what baffled him the first time he watched NFL

 Christian Bale adds NFL legend Al Davis to his rich canon of movie roles with "Madden." The Oscar winner talks football, Thanksgiving and "Heat 2."
 Brian Truitt USA TODAY Updated Nov. 18, 2026, 6:16 p.m. ET Hear this story Christian Bale was thrown particularly by one aspect of American football when he watched it as a kid.
 As a longtime soccer fan, the Welsh-born, English-raised actor was used to the European brand of football being a continuous game, so he was "a little bit stunned" seeing his first NFL game. "I watched it live going, ‘Wait, they're stopping a lot.’ There's a lot of stopping that I didn't really comprehend,” Bale says.
 He came around to enjoying the gridiron and immerses himself in it playing legendary NFL owner Al Davis in director David O. Russell's “Madden” (streaming Nov. 18 on Prime Video ). The sports biopic centers on John Madden (Nicolas Cage) as he coaches the Oakland Raiders to a Super Bowl victory in the 1970s and then retires, becoming an iconic TV color commentator and a video-game pioneer. The movie also focuses on Madden and Davis’ evolving relationship, from coworkers and best friends to frequent foils.

Sign up to receive USA TODAY's movie and TV recommendations right in your inbox “I was aware of John Madden, just sort of in passing, as this avuncular character that people loved. But Al Davis, I didn't know,” says Bale, 52, who lives in LA – a one-time home for the Raiders – with his wife Sibi Blažić and two kids. After doing some research on YouTube (“That’s the only university I ever go to,” Bale quips), it became clear to the Oscar winner that Davis was a singular "brilliant" personality and another in a rich canon of movie roles.
 Watch it here: Stream your favorite shows, the biggest blockbusters and more. "The more I got to know about him, the more I just wanted to keep playing him," he adds. "Giving up playing him was a sad day."
 Bale talks with USA TODAY about portraying Davis, the pressure of starring in “Heat 2” and what’s on his Thanksgiving table.
 This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

Did that kind of scrappiness inform how you played him in “Madden” ? 
 Christian Bale: Absolutely. The man is so scrappy, there's not a fight he ever backed down from, and he would say how his dad insisted on that when he was growing up. Al tried his hand at being an athlete when he was younger, but I think he learned very quickly that he was more of a mind for sports. He knew what he wanted to do his whole life, and he did it, and he never wavered, and he never stopped wanting to do that.
 The thing that he didn't broadcast ever was just what a big heart he had. He truly believed “Once a Raider, always a Raider,” and he took care of people who had not played for the Raiders for years. He made sure they were good, and he checked in on their families, and he loved bringing in outcasts and misfits and troublemakers. He felt himself to be a troublemaker, and he loved that. Good trouble. 
 What was the key for you in capturing that inimitable Davis presence and swagger?  
 Well, the instant thing was this Brooklyn accent but with a Southern twang. Straight away, I was going, “Wait, where did he get that from?” He didn't get it from going to the South. Like so much to do with Al, it's just him."
 You’ve been in boxing and racing movies. Are you a big sports guy? 
 When I was very young, yeah, with soccer, a little bit of rugby. But then I moved around too much, so I could never stay on any one team. So I became more of a smoking behind the bike sheds bloke at school and not really doing the sports. But motorsports I always loved (like) Formula One. The only thing I really watch all the time is MotoGP. And boxing when I was younger: Oh, I loved that (late ‘80s/early ‘90s) era of Nigel Benn and Chris Eubank. And who didn't love watching (Mike) Tyson?
 Al Davis' life motto was “Just win, baby.” What is Christian Bale’s? 
 You know what? I have lots of mottos, I don't really share them. Unlike Al, he liked to broadcast all of that all the time. I think it's bad news to tell people what your motto is. I’ll share it with my kids and my wife and whatnot. You know, there's one that I do like, though, which I think Al would approve of as well: “Resist much, obey little” by Walt Whitman. I have sayings that I repeat to myself every day, and I do create different sayings and mottos for every character I play. I always have a sort of block of them.
 You next star in the prequel/sequel “Heat 2,” playing a younger version of Al Pacino’s LA cop Vincent Hanna. Do you go back and rewatch the original or do your own thing with something like that? 
 I'm obsessively watching it and making sure that it's my Hanna but paying respect, of course, to his Hanna. It’s such an iconic movie, you've got to find that balance. I'm trying to figure it out.
 Thanksgiving is the holiday most synonymous with John Madden. What does Turkey Day look like in your household? 
 I hope we'll have a turducken this year, that’d be great. I've never actually eaten one of those. We had them on the set, but they’d sort of been sitting around for 12 hours and cold by the time I was going to eat it, so I thought no. Whichever family is around or friends who don't have anywhere to go to, that's what Thanksgiving looks like for us.
 Do you have a favorite Thanksgiving side dish ?
 It's not a Thanksgiving thing, but if you put sausages in front of me, I'm always excited. Sausages and ketchup.
